- RESOLUTION AND SILENCE (Finding 036): Kim drove a few miles into the Florida panhandle, asked a stranger 'Is this Florida?', and turned around. A log that samples at fill-ups cannot see it. A record's RESOLUTION sets the floor on what its silences can mean.
- ★★★ THE STATE COUNT IS THE CHAPTER'S BEST EXAMPLE. Kim: 49 mainland states, 10 provinces, and he went out of his way for the awkward ones. The log witnesses 45. THE FOUR IT MISSES SHOW THREE DIFFERENT KINDS OF SILENCE:
  * DELAWARE -- recoverable by geometry. Colonial Heights VA -> Bellmawr NJ reads 264 odometer miles (great-circle 219); the only Delaware-free road is ~305, forty more than the odometer permits. Present as a DISTANCE, absent as a NAME.
  * RHODE ISLAND -- strongly indicated, not forced. 2014-05-17 Bellmawr NJ -> Douglas MA is 287 mi (great-circle 232); the coastal I-95 route through Providence is ~285, the inland route ~265. And Douglas MA sits ON MA-146, the Providence-Worcester road, five miles from the line.
  * FLORIDA -- THE CHAPTER'S BEST SEQUENCE, because it ends in recovery rather than a shrug. THREE kinds of evidence, acquired in the reverse order of their strength:
      1. TESTIMONY (unfalsifiable): a few miles into the panhandle, 'Is this Florida?' 'Yes.' That's all I needed.
      2. INCIDENTAL KNOWLEDGE (falsifiable, survives -- Finding 044): STYX RIVER ROAD. A friend in Alaska lives on the only other one; Kim remembers seeing the Alabama one -- 'Huh? Another one???' -- near the line. 'How would I have known that except by a visit?' A fact he had no reason to want; its uselessness certifies it.
      3. A GEOTAGGED PHOTOGRAPH (documentary): 30.983392, -87.571312 -- N Pineville Rd x Rease Seales Rd, a DEAD END sign and a farm mailbox. ONE AND A FIFTH MILES INSIDE FLORIDA, 5.4 miles from the Atmore fill. Checkable against Street View. FIGURE: images/TwoRed/twored_florida_corner.jpg (KIM TO PLACE THE FILE).
      AND THE ARITHMETIC AGREES: the whole visit is ~11 miles hung off a fuel stop, and the New Orleans -> Atmore segment carries 210 odometer miles against ~195 direct.
      ★★★ THE POINT (Finding 045): Finding 036 was RIGHT -- the fuel log cannot see this. What it does NOT license is 'therefore it is unrecordable,' which is what I wrote. IT WAS UNRECORDABLE BY THAT LOG. He was carrying another instrument that samples on a different trigger -- not 'I bought fuel' but 'this is worth looking at.' A SILENCE BELONGS TO AN INSTRUMENT, NOT TO THE PAST.

  * SOUTH DAKOTA -- recovered 2026-08-21, and the best story of the four. Kim went north from Nebraska on a narrow rural road for the sole purpose of crossing the line, met A CONVOY OF STORM CHASERS coming the other way, crossed, turned around and left. The record holds it as 255 odometer miles where the direct road is ~175 -- ratio 1.83, THE MOST INDIRECT STRETCH IN SIXTEEN YEARS -- on the northern road through Chadron NE, twelve miles from the border.
  * AND THE CHAPTER SHOULD ADMIT MY OWN ERROR HERE, because it is the same lesson one level up: I first reported that no leg had room for South Dakota. The arithmetic was right and the HYPOTHESIS was wrong -- I had assumed visiting a state meant going somewhere IN it. A negative result is only as strong as the hypothesis it tested.
- Key to a ROW, never a LABEL.
- RETIRED RESULTS: the temperature effect died as the sample grew (n=94 -0.068 p=0.045; n=125 -0.050 p=0.099; p=0.17 with controls). The record is now good enough to RETIRE a result, not just produce one.
- THE SIGNAL THAT CANNOT BE SETTLED: a ~3 MPG southern economy deficit, unstable across subsamples, n=30 -- and Creamsicle has ZERO southern fills, so the sample is closed and will not grow. Print the fact that it cannot be settled, not the coefficient.
- THE WITNESS AS AN INSTRUMENT (Findings 039, 041): content reliable, index not. Roads and counts survive decades; what slips is the binding of a memory to an occasion. And a fuel row is a TRANSACTION, not a STATE.
